fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s verified figures are: 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year

behaviours.excerpt: For S5, the proposed 8-per-100,000 recall trigger is above Northwind’s company-wide rate (8.6), but the trigger is model-specific; Hearth 10 is 6.4.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a written incident report and available investigation findings within 10 calendar days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a model-specific hazard or a need to stop use, inspect, or repair a unit.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market release and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and regulator review; a model may not be marketed only if the regulator determines, after review, that corrective measures are inadequate to address an unacceptable safety risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off beginning 12 months after adoption. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers must provide a compatible shut-off upgrade or other regulator-approved equivalent within 72 months, where technically feasible; customers must be notified of any units that cannot be upgraded and the available risk-reduction measures.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A verified model rate above 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year triggers regulator review and a mandatory recall unless the regulator determines, based on documented evidence, that an equally protective corrective action resolves the risk. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material model-specific hazards and provide instructions for inspection, repair, or stopping use.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict with 24-hour reporting and 48-hour customer notice. S2 sets 55°C testing and a 5% review threshold but no automatic sales stop, allowing open-ended corrective action and keeping per-model rates from public disclosure while giving them to customers. S3 requires new-unit shut-off in 12 months and retrofit in 72 months with a feasibility escape. S4 requires built-in suppression in 36 months. S5 sets an 8/100k recall trigger but allows open-ended corrective action and 'prompt' notices.
